notes: rules are documented facts and carry sources. strategies and scoring are this plugin's heuristics for ranking candidates, not facts.
A candidate path is built from: generation boundaries (7 and 8), documented hops, the closest-LTS rule, and minimum-from constraints in versions.json.

strategies.description: Upgrade the existing project and database in place in one major step.
Upgrade the existing project and database in place through intermediate majors.
New codebase on a modern version; the existing database is carried and migrated through intermediate versions. Code and templates are reimplemented.
New installation of the target; content moved by a transfer tool or by hand; code ported. Tool support is verified per project.

rules.description: Upgrade to the closest LTS major before upgrading to a later major.

fact.evidence: You must upgrade to the closest
fact.note: The 17 docs state the same rule for 10 (stop at 13 before 14). For 10 to 13 the closest LTS is the target, so the upgrade is direct.

rules.description: Upgrade to a new major in place by updating the NuGet packages and the target framework.

fact.evidence: You can upgrade to a new major version of Umbraco CMS directly by using NuGet

rules.description: Minor upgrades within Umbraco 7 in place through NuGet (UmbracoCms package).

fact.evidence: how to upgrade to the next minor version when using Umbraco 7

rules.description: Minor upgrades within Umbraco 8 in place through NuGet (UmbracoCms package).

fact.evidence: how to upgrade to the next minor version when using Umbraco 8

rules.description: Minor upgrades within one major from 9 on, in place through NuGet (Umbraco.Cms package).

fact.evidence: NuGet installs the latest version of the package when you use the dotnet add package command unless you specify a package version

rules.description: Umbraco 9 upgrades to 10 in place; SQL CE is not supported from 10.

fact.evidence: The upgrade path between Umbraco 9 and Umbraco 10 can be done directly by upgrading your project using NuGet

rules.description: No in-place upgrade from 7 to 8: migrate the content into a new Umbraco 8 installation and rewrite the code.

landingFact.evidence: Migrate to version 8.5 as a first step
landingFact.note: Documented workaround for a migration introduced in 8.6 that can break the content migration: migrate to 8.5, then upgrade within 8. The other documented workaround is a community package (verify before use).

fact.evidence: There is no direct upgrade path from Umbraco 7 to Umbraco 8

rules.description: No in-place upgrade from 8 to 9: reuse the 8 database in a new Umbraco 9 project and reimplement code and templates.

fact.evidence: You can reuse your content by restoring your Umbraco 8 database into a new database used for an Umbraco 9 site

rules.description: Recommended route from 8: reuse the 8 database in a new Umbraco 10 project (10 carries the 8 migrations), reimplement code and templates, then upgrade majors.

prerequisiteFact.evidence: A Umbraco 8 project running the latest version of Umbraco 8

rules.description: Umbraco 14 replaced the AngularJS backoffice and removed several editors and features. The upgrade stays in place, but affected extensions and content need migration.

removals.text: AngularJS backoffice extensions must be rewritten for the new backoffice.

fact.evidence: Angular JS has been removed in Umbraco 14

removals.text: Nested Content and Grid Layout were removed: rebuild with Block List or Block Grid.

fact.evidence: Nested Content and Grid Layout have been removed

removals.text: The legacy Media Picker was removed: use the default Media Picker.

fact.evidence: The legacy Media Picker has been removed

removals.text: Macros and partial view macros were removed: use partial views or blocks in the rich text editor.

fact.evidence: Macros and partial views macros have been removed in Umbraco 14

removals.text: Smidge was removed: remove its tag helper and injection from _ViewImports.cshtml.

fact.evidence: In Umbraco 14, Smidge has been removed from the CMS

removals.text: Remove the UseInstallerEndpoints call from Program.cs.

fact.evidence: Remove u.UseInstallerEndpoints(); from the program.cs file
Angular JS has been removed in Umbraco 14

rules.description: SQL CE is not supported from Umbraco 10, and there is no official migration path to another engine.
options: convert the SQL CE database to SQL Server with a community guide
create a new database and transfer document types and content with uSync
create a new database and copy the data with a data-compare tool
create a new database and transfer document types and content with Umbraco Deploy

fact.evidence: There is no official migration path from SQL CE to another database engine

rules.description: The content migration from 7 to 8 supports only SQL Server and SQL CE databases.

fact.evidence: The database types that are supported are SQL Server and SQL CE
fact.note: Umbraco 8 does not support MySQL. LocalDB is SQL Server.

scoring.reason: Integer IDs in code and configuration survive only when the database is preserved.
SQL against core tables depends on the existing schema and IDs.
Custom tables live in the CMS database and need a separate transfer when the database is not preserved.
Content-model files (for example uSync or Deploy) make content-transfer tools viable.
A SQL CE database must be converted, with no official tooling, before Umbraco 10.

scoring.mandatoryWork: Rewrite AngularJS backoffice extensions as extensions of the new backoffice. This applies to every strategy.
scoring.reason: AngularJS was removed in Umbraco 14 (rule boundary.13-14).

scoring.mandatoryWork: Convert Nested Content data to Block List or Block Grid.
scoring.reason: Nested Content was removed in Umbraco 14 (rule boundary.13-14).

scoring.mandatoryWork: Convert Grid Layout content to Block Grid.
scoring.reason: Grid Layout was removed in Umbraco 14 (rule boundary.13-14).

scoring.mandatoryWork: Replace macros with partial views or rich text blocks; check rich text content for macro markup first.
scoring.reason: Macros were removed in Umbraco 14 (rule boundary.13-14).
